llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent with its startup-program automation purpose, but it uses browser session cookies and has risky install-time side effects that warrant review before installation.

dimensions.detail: YC commands extract browser cookies from Chrome/Safari/Firefox, auto-discover Chrome profiles on macOS, advise persistent Keychain approval, and merge cookies from startupschool.org and account.ycombinator.com before sending them to Startup School.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The npm postinstall hook automatically creates ~/.claude/skills/yc-cli, removes an existing symlink or recursively deletes an existing non-symlink path at that location, and rewrites installed @steipete/sweet-cookie dependency files under node_modules.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The docs disclose cookie use and submission commands, but the agent workflows encourage generating, filling, validating, and then submitting application files without requiring a separate explicit confirmation immediately before state-changing actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package persists itself into Claude Code's skill directory and mutates a credential-handling dependency during installation; uninstall only removes a matching symlink and cannot restore content deleted or replaced during postinstall.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose covers YC dashboard/update automation, a16z Speedrun applications, SPC form automation, and program discovery, and the code largely implements those features; however, it can submit account updates, submit applications, upload decks, and transmit sensitive founder/company data to third-party services.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Only use it if you are comfortable granting an agent access to your YC browser session, allowing it to submit updates or applications on your behalf, and accepting install-time changes under ~/.claude/skills. Prefer dry runs and manual review before any submission, avoid persistent Keychain approval where possible, and back up or inspect any existing ~/.claude/skills/yc-cli path before installation.
llm.findings:
[YR1] expected: The cookie-access signature is supported by the artifact, but it reflects the documented YC authentication approach rather than evidence of an unrelated stealer or attacker-controlled exfiltration.
[TP4] expected: Speedrun and SPC submissions are purpose-aligned and documented, but they involve sensitive founder, company, fundraising, and attachment data being sent externally.
[PE3] unexpected: Browser cookie decryption is expected for this auth design, but advising users to choose persistent Keychain approval broadens future credential access beyond a one-time command need.
[LP1] unexpected: The skill plainly performs networked CLI workflows, but the frontmatter only lists Bash, Read, and Write, so the effective network behavior is under-declared in the skill permissions.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The install-time symlink setup and dependency patching are not necessary for the core CLI behavior and create non-obvious local side effects.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Natural-language agent examples include submitting updates and applications without documenting a hard confirmation boundary for mutating operations.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The README and skill mention cookies and submissions, but the warnings are not prominent enough for browser-session access and third-party transmission of application data.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Lifecycle hooks automatically alter the local Claude skill directory and can replace existing content at a fixed path during install.
[T09] unexpected: The static findings are supported for cross-domain cookie merging/forwarding and destructive replacement of an existing skill directory; neither appears attacker-directed, but both are material security concerns.
[T07] unexpected: The postinstall script mutates a credential-handling dependency with string replacements; no exfiltration payload was found, but it weakens dependency integrity and auditability.
